whatIs: Tactile UI is a set of components with real physics that behave like hardware objects, for example a PIN screen, an odometer or a dial with detents. It includes 39 interactive objects, 59 page sections, a 217-piece kit and 26 templates, for React, Vue, Svelte or plain JavaScript.
It's a good fit when you want a memorable interface with a tactile feel. If you work with AI agents, it also offers an MCP server so they can use the components directly.
uses: Giving a PIN or code form a screen with realistic physics.
Building a landing page with pre-designed hero, pricing and footer sections.
Installing components through shadcn or letting an AI agent use them through the MCP server.
caveats: Only part of the catalog is free; the rest requires a paid pass.
Components with physics mean continuous animation, so check performance on low-end devices.

The free pieces that ask for an account are only for personal projects; client or commercial work requires a pass. Six pieces, such as the odometer and the compass, are MIT and don't have that restriction.
pricingNote: 62 pieces are free; the full pass is a one-time payment, with a limited-time launch price of $99.
idealFor: Projects that want interfaces with a physical feel and a broad catalog.
